title: Nested ideals inside a regular-sequence ideal under finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $K\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be ideals. Suppose $J$ is generated by a finite $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Suppose also that $A/J$, as an $A/K$-module through the quotient map, has finite Tor dimension: there exists an integer $d\geq0$ such that $\operatorname{Tor}^{A/K}_i(A/J,N)=0$ for every $A/K$-module $N$ and every integer $i>d$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Then $K$ is generated by a finite $A$-regular sequence and $J/K$ is generated by a finite $(A/K)$-regular sequence. All sequences lie in their respective maximal ideals, and empty sequences are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), with finite Tor dimension written using ordinary module Tor; the proof uses Tag 09PV (lemma-injective).

proof.text: Choose an $A$-regular generating sequence $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ for $J$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-trf-lift-regular-generators-through-fibre] with both rings equal to $A$, the map $c=\mathrm{id}_A$, and both its ideals equal to $J$. All local, residue-field and generator-space maps are identities. Its residue-basis assertion says that $([y_i])_{i=1}^r$ is a $k$-basis of $J/\mathfrak mJ$.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), used through its existing local-ring consequence; compare dpa.tex Tag 09PW, minimal generators.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-tor-ideal-generators-injective] to the given ideals $K\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Its Tor bound is precisely the hypothesis of the item. Thus $\beta:K/\mathfrak mK\to J/\mathfrak mJ$, $[x]\mapsto[x]$, is injective.

By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose finitely many generators of $K$. Their residues span $K/\mathfrak mK$: reduce any linear expression modulo $\mathfrak m$. Scan this finite spanning list, retaining a vector exactly when it is outside the span of the previously retained ones. At each insertion, a relation with nonzero new coefficient would express the new vector in the old span; hence the retained list is independent and still spans at the end. Denote this basis by $[f_1],\ldots,[f_s]$, using the chosen generators as lifts in $K$.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), choice of minimal generators; elementary finite spanning-list reduction.

proof.text: The vectors $\beta([f_i])$ are independent: apply injectivity of $\beta$ to a relation and then independence of the $[f_i]$. Scan $[y_1],\ldots,[y_r]$ and append a vector exactly when it is outside the current span. The same insertion argument as in Step 3 preserves independence, and the final span contains every $[y_j]$, hence is all of $J/\mathfrak mJ$. This yields an ordered basis beginning with $[f_1],\ldots,[f_s]$; its added vectors have lifts among the $y_j$. Write the added lifts as $f_{s+1},\ldots,f_r$. The two bases have the same number of vectors by [lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality], applied in both directions (each list is independent and its underlying set spans). Thus the extended list has $r$ vectors. In particular $s\leq r$.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), extension to a minimal generating list of J; explicit finite basis extension.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] for the finite module $K$, its basis lifts $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ generate $K$. Apply [lem-trf-lift-regular-generators-through-fibre] again with $R=S=A$, $c=\mathrm{id}_A$ and both ideals $J$. Its assertion for every lifted basis applies to the list of Step 4, so $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ is an $A$-regular sequence generating $J$. This uses the statement of that node, including regularity, rather than only its residue-basis clause.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), final sentences; regularity of the replacement generators through More on Algebra Tags 066A and 09CC, and Algebra Tag 00DV.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $A/K$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/K$. From [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], the prefix $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ has the required injective multiplications; its final quotient $A/K$ is nonzero, so it is regular. The images of $f_{s+1},\ldots,f_r$ generate $J/K$. After quotienting by the first $t$ of these images the ring is $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_{s+t})$: both equivalence relations identify representatives whose difference belongs to this ideal. Multiplication by the next image is exactly multiplication by $f_{s+t+1}$ on this ring, hence injective. The final quotient is $A/J\ne0$ since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus the tail is regular over $A/K$. All $f_i\in J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and tail images lie in $\mathfrak m/K$. If $s=0$ or $s=r$ the corresponding list is empty, with nonzero final quotient as above; $r=0$ gives $J=K=0$.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), conclusion from the chosen regular list; prefix and quotient calculation, with Algebra Tags 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring) and 07BJ (lemma-characterize-local-ring-map) for local structure.

lean.statement: theorem exists_regular_generators_nested_of_finite_tor {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (K J : Ideal A) (hKJ : K ≤ J) (hJ : J ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hreg : ∃ ys : List A, Ideal.ofList ys = J ∧ IsRegular A ys) (hTor : ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ K)) (i : ℕ), d < i → IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ K)) i).obj ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Ideal.Quotient.factor hKJ)).obj (ModuleCat.of (A ⧸ J) (A ⧸ J)))).obj N)) : (∃ fs : List A, Ideal.ofList fs = K ∧ IsRegular A fs ∧ ∀ f ∈ fs, f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ∧ (∃ gs : List (A ⧸ K), Ideal.ofList gs = J.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk K) ∧ IsRegular (A ⧸ K) gs ∧ ∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk K))
